description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
package: dev board, on its own carrier (PCB-MATRIX-CARRIER) hung from the oak top, its pad rows on HDR-MATRIX
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 17 GPIO on its two pad rows (1-7, 33-40, 43, 44) and 12 used. MOUNTED ON ITS OWN CARRIER BOARD (owner, 2026-10-03, option (c); ADR 0021 amendment 2026-10-03): two 1x10 headers (HDR-MATRIX) join its pad rows to the carrier (PCB-MATRIX-CARRIER), which hangs from the oak top on three spacers (MECH-MX-*), and CBL-MCU-RIBBON runs from the carrier's J-MCU-C to J-MCU. ONLY ITS PAD ROWS ARE WIRED: it is programmed and recovered over its own USB-C, with its BOOT and RESET buttons (owner, 2026-10-03: 'Program over USB only'), and its pad-row 5V and GND carry its supply, so no back-side pad (TP2, TP3, EN, IO0) is wired. Its USB-C is the instrument's USB port, by the panel-mount extension to the tail face (mechanical/DESIGN.md); NO ESD ARRAY on that path, by the owner's decision (ADR 0021 amendment 2026-10-02): the Matrix's own D+/D- reach the ESP32-S3 with nothing between [ds WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf, USB block]. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM, both on-package: the vendor schematic marks U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2 [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; F=in-package flash, H4=4MB, R2=2MB quad PSRAM from Espressif's ordering code, from memory], so GPIO33-37 are free - octal PSRAM would have taken them. The 8x8 matrix is the instrument's only display, under a window in the top face (ADR 0015) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003). THE SENSOR IS SOLDERED TO THE BOARD AND COATED WITH IT: a sensor swap breaks the coating at its eight joints - re-mask both ports before touching it up

part: 4-layer PCB - the main board: thumb switches, both thumb registers and the carrier circuits
description: Thumb switches and their registers, breath sensor, reference, ADC, umbilical, SPI egress, LED drive and the LED row, the regulator, service header
package: long and narrow, sized in mechanical/drc.echo (main board), 1.6mm (config/body.yaml switch.pcb_t)
notes: ONE board at the thumb level, mouth cap to the end of the right hand (ADR 0017). A TONGUE runs on from its tail end to the etherCON's adapter and carries J-UMB, soldered into both (ADR 0021). The thumb switches solder into it; the key boards connect to it by 12-conductor IDC ribbons (CBL-CHAIN), a through-hole right-angle J-CHAIN header for each in its far band beside the LED row. Parts face up - mechanical/drc.echo gives the room under the key boards and elsewhere. A clearance hole for each U-bolt leg, no edge notches, and a plated PWR_GND hole at each mount, every one on the cassette's bottom plate: the stud, the spacer, the board, then a column's standoff or an end mount's nut (ADR 0022, ADR 0025). Its underside faces the grounded bottom plate over its whole length, so an underside part needs a window cut in the plate (hardware/boards/main-board/README.md). 1.6mm, as the key boards, its top pressed against the thumb switches' housing bottom (ADR 0020 Amendment 6). Long: check the board house's panel and price before M4. FOUR LAYERS, signal / ground / power / signal (ADR 0017 amendment 2026-09-29): layer 2 the PWR_GND plane with the analog island, power-entry-instrument.md section 2. WHITE SOLDER MASK, both faces (owner, ADR 0028): the top face is the LED row's first reflector. ASSEMBLY: JLCPCB assembles the parts whose sheet field Assembly is machine (the SMT passives, ICs and the LED row). HAND-SOLDERED, Assembly=hand on the sheets: the thumb switches (SW1-n), the through-hole headers J-CHAIN x2, J-UMB, J-MCU and HDR-SERVICE, the U-BUCK module (THT SIP) and the breath sensor U-BREATH. The Matrix (U-MCU-RT) is on its own carrier board (PCB-MATRIX-CARRIER), not this one: CBL-MCU-RIBBON reaches it from J-MCU. OPEN UNTIL tools/kicad.py check passes on hardware/boards/main-board and its fab/ is re-exported from the passing board

part: 2x12 1.27mm shrouded box header, right-angle, keyed (XKB X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01)
description: The Matrix's connector on the main board: CBL-MCU-RIBBON from the Matrix carrier's J-MCU-C plugs in here, and unplugs with the lid raised
notes: PART: XKB X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01, LCSC C5147255, through-hole right-angle, keyed and shrouded, all gold flash, 1A per contact [ds connectors/XKB-X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01.pdf]; the sheet carries it, footprint drawn from that drawing (hardware/lib/README.md). Mates the Yxcon IDC3-24232A1AUC1 sockets of CBL-MCU-RIBBON - a standard 1.27mm IDC fit, confirm on the first pair. WHERE: config/body.yaml boards.mcu_conn_at, off the LED row at the near edge, its mouth toward the far side (mechanical/export/pcb-geometry.echo 'J-MCU'), J-MCU-C straight above it under the Matrix carrier, so the ribbon rises from one socket's back to the other's. PINOUT (ADR 0018), ribbon conductor n = pin n, odd and even across the two rows, pin 1 where XKB's drawing and JLC's footprint put it (hardware/lib/README.md): 1 5V, 2 GND, 3 5V, 4 IO1, 5 IO2 (spare), 6 IO7, 7 IO3 (spare), 8 IO38, 9 GND, 10 IO35, 11 GND, 12 IO36, 13 3V3, 14 IO34, 15 GND, 16 IO39, 17 5V, 18 IO37, 19 IO33, 20 IO40, 21 IO44 (RX), 22 IO43 (TX), 23 and 24 on no net (IO0 and EN until the owner chose to program the Matrix over its own USB-C only, 2026-10-03). hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative. Every fast line - IO35 SCLK, IO36 MOSI, IO34 CS_MOD, IO38 chain SCK, IO7 SH/LD - has a ground, a supply or a static line on both sides; pin 9 is the ground between SCLK (IO35) and the chain clock (IO38). IO2 and IO3 are spare and reach no other part on the main board; bring them to two test pads beside J-MCU. KEYED AND SHROUDED: a reversed plug puts 5V on a GPIO. RATING: the 5V and GND contacts carry the whole Matrix draw, and fed from the 5V pad nothing on the Matrix limits it (its USB diode is bypassed - matrix-led-current, power_path), so rate them against U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0), not against matrix-led-current: three 5V contacts at ~0.33A and four GND at ~0.25A each [calc, equal sharing], against the header's and the socket's 1A per contact [ds XKB-X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01.pdf; YXCON-IDC3-24232A1AUC1-1.27MM-IDC-SOCKET.pdf].

part: 24-way flat ribbon, 0.635mm pitch, with a 2x12 1.27mm IDC socket at each end
description: The Matrix's wiring: J-MCU-C on the Matrix carrier to J-MCU on the main board
notes: CONDUCTORS: 24, conductor n = J-MCU pin n = J-MCU-C pin 25-n (J-MCU row; hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative, the Matrix carrier's sheet is held to it by tools/kicad.py check); conductors 23 and 24 carry nothing. SOCKETS: two Yxcon IDC3-24232A1AUC1 [ds YXCON-IDC3-24232A1AUC1-1.27MM-IDC-SOCKET.pdf], one each end, keyed. J-MCU-C is the same header as J-MCU hung upside down from the Matrix carrier, so the CARRIER SOCKET IS CRIMPED TURNED OVER: its pin 1 on conductor 24, the main-board socket's on conductor 1. Both keys then face their headers' slots and the ribbon runs flat between them with no twist; a socket crimped the other way will not go in. CURRENT: at U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0) the three 5V conductors carry ~0.33A each and the four GND ~0.25A [calc, equal sharing]; a 0.635mm conductor carries that without heating to speak of [from memory]. RESISTANCE IS WHAT THE FOUR GROUNDS ARE FOR: ~34mohm per 100mm [from memory, ~30AWG], four in parallel ~8.5mohm per 100mm. The Matrix's 3V3 is the ADC's reference (carrier/breath-adc) and is regulated against the Matrix's ground, so LED return current in these grounds moves it. E11 confirms it: breath output clean while the matrix is exercised. LENGTH: mechanical/drc.echo 'Matrix ribbon length' between the sockets, the lid (which the carrier hangs from) held routing.chain_raise up, as the key chain's; closed it folds flat in four legs between the two headers, short of the LED row's band ('Matrix ribbon closed: its folds between the sockets'). CABLE: 3M 3754 or equal, 0.025 in pitch 30 AWG [ds connectors/3M-3754-FLAT-CABLE-0.025IN-30AWG-PVC.pdf]. A DEAD MATRIX: lift the lid, unplug J-MCU, unscrew the carrier from the oak (three MECH-MX-SCREW), and replace the carrier with the Matrix on it, or desolder the Matrix's headers - nothing on the main board or the key boards is touched

part: 2x12 1.27mm shrouded box header, right-angle, keyed - the same part as J-MCU
description: The Matrix ribbon's carrier end: CBL-MCU-RIBBON from J-MCU plugs in here, on the Matrix carrier's underside
notes: PART: as J-MCU (that row says which, and the sheet's fields carry it). WHERE: hung upside down from the Matrix carrier's arm, straight above J-MCU, its mouth the same way (mechanical/export/pcb-geometry.echo 'matrix' 'J-MCU-C'), so the ribbon rises from one socket's back to the other's. PINOUT: pin k carries J-MCU pin 25-k (CBL-MCU-RIBBON says why); hardware/boards/matrix-carrier/matrix-carrier.kicad_sch is held to hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml by tools/kicad.py check. Pins 1 and 2 (J-MCU 24 and 23) are on no net. Assembly: hand

part: 1x10 2.54mm pin header, straight, surface mount, staggered feet, gold (hanxia HX PZ2.54-1x10P TP-YQ)
description: The Matrix's two pad rows to the Matrix carrier: a header standing on the carrier, through the Matrix's pads
notes: ONE PER PAD ROW, pin 1 at the Matrix's USB-C edge: the 5V..IO1 row and the IO33..RX row [ds WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-pinout.png]; the carrier's sheet names each pin for its pad. PART: hanxia HX PZ2.54-1x10P TP-YQ, LCSC C41417367: plastic 2.5 (config/body.yaml boards.matrix_hdr_h, which the Matrix sits on and which clears its back-side parts - drc.echo 'Matrix's back-side parts clear the carrier'), posts 3.2 above it, staggered feet 5.0 across, gold [ds connectors/HANXIA-HX-PZ2.54-1x10P-TP-YQ.pdf]; JLC 1,090 in stock 2026-10-03. SURFACE MOUNT, NOT THROUGH-HOLE: J-MCU-C hangs under the carrier straight below the 5V..IO1 row's first pins, and a through-hole tail there would stand in its insulator. Type A (YQ) only; the footprint is that type's. BUILD: both headers soldered to the carrier's top face (by hand or JLC's assembly), the Matrix down onto their posts and seated on the plastic, its top face flat; solder both ends, then CUT THE POSTS FLUSH ON THE MATRIX'S TOP FACE and keep the joints flat - its top rises into the oak's shallow relief (openings.matrix_relief_d). IO4, IO5 and IO6 reach nothing and are soldered for strength. Assembly: hand

description: Holds the Matrix on HDR-MATRIX under its window, and J-MCU-C straight above J-MCU
notes: THE MATRIX'S OWN BOARD (owner, 2026-10-03: option (c), a separate small carrier, and 'Hang from the lid'; ADR 0021 amendment 2026-10-03), replacing option (d)'s rails on the right-hand key board, which is back at its original length. The main board's width, under the Matrix and just past it, with a notch round the USB-C receptacle and the plug's overmould (review #19 F1 holds) and an arm forward along the near edge over J-MCU, from which J-MCU-C hangs. Two layers, the key boards' rules and board house, white mask (ADR 0028), one order with them. hardware/boards/matrix-carrier/README.md; ORDERED FROM ITS FAB PACK, hardware/boards/matrix-carrier/fab/, held to the board by tools/kicad.py check
